A cross-section diagram showing three enlarged soil particles. The first particle has a very thick layer of water around it with a downward arrow. The second shows water filling the small gaps between particles, with a root hair absorbing it. The third shows a very thin, tightly bound dark blue ring of water completely surrounding a dry particle,.

A four-part diagram showing the progression of water erosion. Panel 1: "Splash" showing a raindrop hitting soil and soil particles splashing out. Panel 2: "Sheet" showing a flat layer of muddy water running off a slope. Panel 3: "Rill" showing small, narrow channels forming in the soil. Panel 4: "Gully" showing a deep, wide, V-shaped trench cutting through the landscape.

A four-panel diagram showing the types of irrigation. 1. Surface (Furrow): water flowing in trenches between ridges of crops. 2. Sub-surface: underground pipes releasing moisture to roots. 3. Sprinkler: rotating nozzle spraying water over a field of crops. 4. Drip: black plastic pipes on the surface dripping water exactly at the base of tomato plants.
